newsitem.title: USA: Chicago mayor says talks ongoing with Illinois.
newsitem.headline: Chicago mayor says talks ongoing with Illinois.

text.p: A report in a Chicago newspaper Wednesday tying state legislation over a city airport to a domed stadium and the passage of a state bond authorization bill elicited a comment from Chicago Mayor Richard Daley that talks were ongoing with Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar on "a wide-range of issues."
A spokesman for Edgar also confirmed that state officials were talking with the city.

The Chicago Sun-Times reported that Edgar's signing Monday of a bill allowing the state to takeover Meigs Field on Chicago's downtown lakefront, double-crossed the Daley Administration in talks with the state.
Those talks, according to the paper, included an agreement for the state to drop its lawsuits to block city plans to turn the airport into a $27 million, bond-financed nature park.

In return, the newspaper said the governor would get a multi-pupose domed stadium in Chicago for use by the Chicago Bears football team and by conventions, as well as the mayor's help in getting Democratic lawmakers to agree to support a $610 million general obligation bond authorization bill that the Republican governor wants.

However, a statement from Daley said the question of whether or not Edgar would sign the Meigs Field bill into law "was never a part of these discussions, which have been held in a spirit of compromise and cooperation."
Mike Lawrence, Edgar's spokesman, also said that the governor's signing of the bill had nothing to do with any discussions.
"That (Edgar) broke a deal is totally, absolutely wrong," Lawrence said.
Neither Lawrence nor Lisa Howard, a spokeswoman for Daley, would comment on what exactly was being discussed between city and state officials.
